exchangeRate.trend: ▬ Holding; disaster and session politics in focus
exchangeRate.contextHtml: The peso stayed in the low-₱61 range through June 20 as Congress returned for a Marcos-called special session and Mindanao reconstruction costs climbed past ₱1.35 billion in reported infrastructure damage.

articles.headline: Gatchalian Elected Senate President as Villanueva Delivers 13th Vote; Cayetano Concedes
articles.descriptionHtml: During a June 17 special session called by President Marcos, Sherwin Gatchalian was formally elected Senate president with all 13 senators present voting for him after Joel Villanueva joined the majority—supplying the constitutional threshold Cayetano’s bloc had denied since the June 3 quorum of 12. The Cayetano-led minority skipped the morning session; Alan Peter Cayetano conceded defeat shortly before the vote. The session also convened the Commission on Appointments to confirm 85 ambassadors and 5 generals. Cayetano had filed a Supreme Court petition June 16 seeking to void the June 3 reorganization, but the chamber moved on. Gatchalian inherits a divided Senate weeks before Vice President Sara Duterte’s July 6 impeachment trial—ending a monthlong leadership crisis that began with Cayetano’s May 11 takeover and Bato dela Rosa’s May 13 Senate standoff.
articles.diasporaImpact: A settled Senate presidency clears the path for impeachment logistics; overseas observers can finally track one official calendar for Sara Duterte’s trial.

articles.headline: Marcos Special Session Targets Anti-Dynasty Bill; Sara Pre-Trial Opens With Presiding Officer Still Unsettled
articles.descriptionHtml: President Marcos issued Proclamation No. 1318 on June 15 calling Congress to special session June 17, listing eight priority measures including an anti-political dynasty bill, tertiary-education reforms, and expanded AICS cash aid. The session became the venue for resolving Senate leadership rather than passing the dynasty measure, which Cayetano noted remained at interpellation stage. On June 18 the Sara Duterte impeachment pre-trial conference opened; Gatchalian said he would preside for now while the majority floated Francis Escudero as trial presiding officer—a role senators amended rules to allow in non-presidential impeachments. Gatchalian also said Jinggoy Estrada’s Sandiganbayan preventive suspension bars him from sitting as an impeachment judge during the 90-day window. Both panels agreed to expedite proceedings; document marking resumes Monday. The week bridged Marcos’s governance agenda and the impeachment clock.
articles.diasporaImpact: Anti-dynasty legislation matters to overseas voters tracking whether dynastic concentration ever faces a statutory cap; pre-trial rules determine if unexplained-wealth evidence reaches open Senate testimony.

articles.headline: PH-US Fourth Maritime Drill Completes Near Bajo de Masinloc as China Removes Floating Platform
articles.descriptionHtml: Philippine and U.S. forces completed their fourth bilateral maritime cooperative activity of 2026 from June 14–19, involving the Navy frigate BRP Diego Silang, PCG vessels, FA-50s, and US Coast Guard cutters near Bajo de Masinloc despite PLA Navy and China Coast Guard presence. Exercises included search-and-rescue, VBSS drills, and division tactics. Separately, NTF-WPS confirmed on June 17 that the Chinese floating platform monitored inside the shoal lagoon since late May was removed after Manila’s diplomatic protest. Beijing’s embassy later called it a completed “research mission.” Manila said removal does not concede Chinese rights and vowed continued patrols. The twin developments—allied presence plus platform withdrawal—mark a tactical WPS win without resolving underlying Scarborough control since the 2012 standoff.
articles.diasporaImpact: Allied drills near Panatag reassure diaspora communities watching China’s lagoon installations; removal is relief, not resolution, for fishers blocked from traditional grounds.

articles.headline: Mindanao Earthquake Toll Climbs to 78; 1.4 Million Affected and ₱1.35B Infrastructure Damage
articles.descriptionHtml: Ten days after the June 8 quake, NDRRMC Situation Report No. 10 recorded 78 deaths, 1,339 injured, and 30 missing, affecting 346,413 families or roughly 1.41 million people across Regions IX, XI, XII, and BARMM. Damaged houses totaled 74,657 (13,681 destroyed); infrastructure damage reached about ₱1.35 billion. 81,855 people remained displaced; power outages persisted in 34 areas and water disruptions in 15. PHIVOLCS logged thousands of aftershocks including a magnitude 6.4 event. Government assistance exceeded ₱176 million. Fourteen LGUs stayed under state-of-calamity declarations. Recovery competed for national attention with the Senate special session—testing whether disaster response stays funded as impeachment politics accelerates.
articles.diasporaImpact: Rising casualty and displacement counts mean remittance spikes and housing rebuild costs will persist for months in Soccsksargen and Davao Occidental hometowns.

items.title: Gatchalian (Valenzuela)
items.bodyHtml: Win Gatchalian went from acting president to constitutionally elected Senate president in one special session—now presiding over both chamber business and Sara Duterte’s pre-trial while Escudero’s trial-judge role remains unsettled.

items.title: Marcos-Romualdez
items.bodyHtml: Marcos used Proclamation 1318 to force Congress back to work—getting a Senate president ally and WPS platform removal in the same week, even as the anti-dynasty bill he listed as priority remained stuck in debate.
